intro: Suggestions for you to review. None is implemented. Choose an option for each decision, and the next session will carry it out. Recommendations are marked; the choice is yours.

decisions.decision: How should the five product links be handled?
options: A. Keep the supplied short links, flagged as unvalidated, until the Associates test passes.
B. Run the Associates test first, then replace links with tagged product URLs (https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=<tracking ID>) only for products that pass.
C. Use only tagged product URLs now, with no short links.
decisions.recommendation: B — validate one link per product first (Associates workflow), then scale. This matches the brief's own sequence.
decisions.trade_offs: A keeps the current links but leaves the compliance question open. B adds one manual test step. C is a guess about the tag format, since the tag was not tested.

decisions.decision: How should pricing and reviews be handled, given §2(b), §6(t) and §6(y)?
options: A. Apply for PA-API / Creators API and show prices and ratings with a 'as of' timestamp, under the policy terms.
B. Link-only: show product title and a link, with no price or rating; the reader sees the price on Amazon.
C. Drop the price-analysis goal.
decisions.recommendation: B now; move to A only after API access is confirmed (Q4).
decisions.trade_offs: A gives richer pages but needs API access and ongoing data upkeep. B is policy-safe today. C removes a brief goal the policy restricts.

decisions.decision: How should clicks and conversions be measured?
options: A. Use only Associates reports (Tracking ID reports). No site-side tracking. Simplest and least data collection.
B. Add a privacy-preserving click counter on a host you control (for example a small serverless function), counting aggregate outbound clicks with no cookies and no IP storage.
C. Add a third-party privacy-focused analytics tool.
decisions.recommendation: A now, then B once the five events are defined (Q5) and a host is chosen (Q6).
decisions.trade_offs: A cannot tell which page sent a click. B needs a host outside GitHub Pages and a privacy notice. C adds a third party to the disclosure list.

decisions.decision: What should the front page emphasise?
options: A. Product-first: the five products as cards, with a short 'what it is' note from the listing title.
B. Category-first: two category pages (Air fryers, Thermometers) with the table on each.
C. Guide-first: lead with buyer-question guides (requires D6).
decisions.recommendation: A, with category pages behind it. Guides come later once the product pages are verified.
decisions.trade_offs: A is quick and accurate but has little editorial depth. C is more editorial but depends on content that is not yet written or verified.

decisions.decision: What publishing cadence should guides follow?
options: A. Weekly, with one guide each week.
B. Every two weeks.
C. Monthly, paired with an Associates-report review.
decisions.recommendation: C — a monthly cadence leaves room to check each guide against Associates reports and Amazon's current policy before publishing.
decisions.trade_offs: A gives more frequent content but multiplies verification work. B is a middle path. C is slower but easier to verify.

decisions.decision: Which working titles should become guides?
options: A. 'Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?'
B. 'A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity'
C. 'How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs'
D. 'Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance'
E. None yet.
decisions.recommendation: Publish A and D first, because they match the products on the site and need no price or rating claims. Hold B and C until product specifications are verified from official listings.
decisions.trade_offs: Each guide must cite only verified facts. Without price or rating data, guides rely on structural differences (basket vs oven, capacity, cleanup) that the owner must verify.

decisions.decision: Which domain should the site use?
options: A. GitHub Pages address (free, no DNS work).
B. Custom domain you own (needs DNS access).
decisions.recommendation: A for launch; add B later if you have a domain.
decisions.trade_offs: A is simplest. B looks more like a publication but needs ownership and DNS.

decisions.decision: How should the site get imagery?
options: A. Text-first design with no product photos.
B. Product images supplied through Amazon's official linking tools (Program Content), used unaltered except resizing.
C. Original illustrations or photos made for the site.
decisions.recommendation: A now; B when the Associates tools provide images for the five products.
decisions.trade_offs: A is safest and fastest. B needs Program Content access. C is effort and must avoid implying Amazon endorsement.

decisions.decision: What visual direction should the site take?
options: A. Magazine: serif headlines, warm neutrals, generous white space.
B. Catalog: clean sans-serif, product grid, strong category bar.
C. Minimal dashboard: the current layout, unchanged.
decisions.recommendation: A for the front page, with the dashboard pages (findings, sources, flagged) kept in plain tables. Matches the brief's 'publication' goal.
decisions.trade_offs: A is more work than C. B fits shopping best but reads more like a store than a publication.

decisions.decision: Who should be named as author?
options: A. A named person you supply (recommended for reader trust).
B. 'Editorial team' with a contact address.
C. No byline.
decisions.recommendation: A, once you supply a real name and role. Do not invent a name.
decisions.trade_offs: A needs your input. B is honest but less personal. C is the least trust-building.

deferred_items.item: Nav labels, RSS feed, Search Console, reader capture
deferred_items.state: Partly done: RSS feed of site updates and sitemap.xml are generated. Search Console and reader capture need your account and decisions (D3, D7).
